title: Book Three · Chapter 133: The Twelfth Morning
story:
Friday is Ronan's twelfth and last morning at the workshop.

He arrives before nine and opens his question sheet. There are a few pencil marks beside the headings now. Mr Sun has used the same sheet twice himself.

Ronan checks the front shelves. He puts the newest drawing with the right customer name, then clears a space on the measuring table.

The morning is busy. He brings water for one waiting woman and finds a paper for another. At the bench, Dad and the other worker continue their own jobs.

Before twelve, Mr Sun comes to the counter with the pay book.

“Four weeks,” he says.

Ronan looks at the twelve dates. Every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday is there.

“Thirty-six hours,” he says.

Mr Sun gives him the last six yuan. Ronan has earned twenty-four altogether. The peanuts cost one, so twenty-three remains from his wages.

He counts today's money and puts it away.

“Thank you,” he says.

Mr Sun nods. “You asked useful questions.”

“I measured from one once.”

“Once was enough.”

They smile. Ronan puts the short pencil beside the paper box and takes his own cloth from the shelf.

Dad comes over before he leaves.

“Your mornings are free again.”

“I might sleep through one.”

“Only one?”

Ronan laughs. Dad gives his shoulder a light touch, then returns to the bench. He still has work after lunch.

At home, Ronan puts the final six with the seventeen. He writes twenty-three on the work envelope. He leaves it in his own place.

That afternoon, he meets Anna in the park. She has spent the morning with her drawings. Now her notebook stays in her bag while they walk.

“What did you like best?” she asks.

Ronan thinks about the shelves and the labels.

“Finding out what people really needed. The cups. The woman's table.”

“And the pay?”

“The pay could stay too.”

She laughs and takes his hand.

He tells her about the little boy and Mr Sun's hair. She stops in the path to laugh, and he waits beside her until she can walk again.

At the turn, she asks about the next week. She and Lin have a morning run planned.

“I can meet you afterward,” he says. “No counter on Monday.”

They choose noon on Monday. Then Anna moves closer in the shade, and they walk on past the field with their hands together.

On Monday, he brings water to the park at noon. Anna comes from her run and sits beside him. He gives her the bottle, then moves his bag so she can rest in the shade.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

pay book＝工资记录本；wages＝工资；altogether＝合计；afterward＝之后。

## 理解问题

1. 四周实际上完多少个上午、多少小时？累计工资和扣除花生后的余额各是多少？
2. Ronan最喜欢工作的哪些部分？四周结束后，Dad和Anna是否仍各有自己的事？

## 读句子

**He writes twenty-three on the work envelope.**

拆开看：He / writes twenty-three / on the work envelope.

他／写下二十三／在装工资的信封上。
